# ============================================================================
# EV Charging Monitor — BYD Shark 6 on Athom Smart Plug V3 (share house)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Home Assistant PACKAGE. Attributes each charge to solar-diverted vs grid and
# computes a fair reimbursement using tiered feed-in valuation.
#
# DESIGN NOTES (why it's built this way):
#  * BILLED kWh is anchored to the plug's HARDWARE cumulative energy register,
#    NOT to a Riemann integral. A Wi-Fi/`unavailable` dropout makes HA's
#    integration hold its last value and bill phantom (or zero) charging; the
#    hardware register is monotonic and drift-free. The two Riemann integrals
#    are used ONLY to derive the solar:grid RATIO, which then rescales the
#    hardware total. `sensor.ev_split_residual_kwh` is a health check on that.
#  * Solar diverted to the car is valued at OPPORTUNITY COST — the feed-in
#    credit the household forwent — at the MARGINAL tier active at that instant.
#  * Conservative by default: no solar data ⇒ 100% grid, so the household is
#    never undercharged.
#
# INSTALL (HA OS, Core 2025.7.3):
#   1. configuration.yaml:
#        homeassistant:
#          packages: !include_dir_named packages
#   2. Copy this file to  /config/packages/ev_charging_monitor.yaml
#   3. Developer Tools > YAML > Check Configuration, then Restart.
#   4. Dashboard: add ev_charging_dashboard.yaml as a new view.
#
# ── TWO THINGS TO SET ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# (A) PLUG ENTITY IDs. Defaults below are the expected ESPHome slugs for node
#     "athom-smart-plug-v3-4cb818". VERIFY in Developer Tools > States (search
#     "athom") and correct them here if different:
#        power        : sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_power             (W)
#        total energy : sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy      (kWh, lifetime)
#        switch       : switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch
# (B) SOLAR — OPTION B ESTIMATE (wired 2026-09-07). The SG5K-D inverter has NO
#     grid meter: the Sungrow iSolarCloud integration exposes PV generation only
#     (no grid import/export/consumption). So solar attribution is ESTIMATED:
#         exportable surplus = max(0, PV_generation − house_baseline)
#         solar_to_car       = min(car_power, surplus)
#     PV source: sensor.inverter1_inverter_ac_power (W).
#     Baseline: input_number.house_baseline_w, default 0 ("take the whole yield",
#     the agreed basis since the solar was unused before Nick arrived). Raise it
#     to carve out the household's own daytime solar use. PV unavailable ⇒ 100%
#     grid (conservative). This is an estimate, not metered export — the dashboard
#     banner says so.
# ============================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# 1. HELPERS  (ISC-1..7)
# ===========================================================================
input_number:
  tariff_consumption:
    name: Tariff — consumption (grid import)
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-import
  tariff_fit_tier1:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power
  tariff_fit_tier2:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 2
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power-variant
  tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1 daily limit
    min: 0
    max: 100
    step: 0.5
    unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:gauge
  # OPTION B (no grid meter): estimate solar surplus as PV generation minus an
  # assumed household background load. 0 = "take the whole PV yield" (the agreed
  # basis, since the solar sat unused before Nick arrived). Raise it later if the
  # household wants their own daytime solar use carved out of the car's share.
  house_baseline_w:
    name: Estimated house baseline load (Option B)
    min: 0
    max: 5000
    step: 50
    unit_of_measurement: "W"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:home-lightning-bolt
  # Session snapshot anchors (set by automation; not for manual use)
  ev_session_energy_start:
    name: EV session energy start (internal)
    min: 0
    max: 1000000
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:database-marker
  ev_session_cost_start:
    name: EV session cost start (internal)
    min: 0
    max: 1000000
    step: 0.0001
    unit_of_measurement: "$"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:database-marker

input_boolean:
  ev_solar_charge_mode:
    name: EV solar-following charge mode
    icon: mdi:weather-sunny
  ev_charge_now:
    name: EV charge now (force plug on)
    icon: mdi:flash

# Display-only pointer to the solar source. Templates use hard constants for
# robustness (dereferencing input_text is fragile), so editing this does NOT
# change behaviour — edit the << SET SOLAR SOURCE >> lines instead.
input_text:
  ev_grid_export_sensor:
    name: EV grid-export source (reference only)
    max: 120
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-export

# ===========================================================================
# 2. TEMPLATE SENSORS + BINARY SENSOR
#    (ISC-9..12, 16..18, 22..25) — one `template:` block (HA forbids two).
#    Availability guards keep dropouts out of the integrals (ISC-36).
# ===========================================================================
template:
  - sensor:
      # -- Plug power, mirrored with a guard (ISC-9) --------------------------
      - name: "EV Car Power W"
        unique_id: ev_car_power_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        availability: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_power')
             not in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] }}
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_power') | float(0) }}

      # -- Exportable solar surplus (ISC-10) — OPTION B ESTIMATE --------------
      #    No grid meter on this SG5K-D (iSolarCloud exposes PV generation only),
      #    so surplus = max(0, PV_generation − assumed house baseline). This is
      #    the energy that would be EXPORTED if the car weren't charging, which
      #    is exactly what the fair-share split needs. Source is the inverter AC
      #    power sensor; baseline is the adjustable helper (default 0 = whole
      #    yield). PV unavailable ⇒ 0 ⇒ split forces 100% grid (conservative,
      #    ISC-35). NOTE: this is an ESTIMATE, not metered export — the dashboard
      #    banner says so.
      - name: "EV Grid Export W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_export_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set v = states('sensor.inverter1_inverter_ac_power') %}
          {% if v in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] %}
            0
          {% else %}
            {% set pv = v | float(0) %}
            {% set base = states('input_number.house_baseline_w') | float(0) %}
            {{ [pv - base, 0] | max }}
          {% endif %}

      # -- Split: solar-to-car / grid-to-car (ISC-11, ISC-12) ----------------
      - name: "EV Solar To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set exp = states('sensor.ev_grid_export_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car, exp] | min }}
      - name: "EV Grid To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car - solar, 0] | max }}

      # -- Counterfactual RUNNING daily export (ISC-16) — the running daily
      #    cumulative the FIT tier boundary is measured against. Under OPTION B
      #    the surplus sensor (ev_grid_export_w) is already the PRE-car exportable
      #    surplus (PV − baseline, car load not subtracted), so its daily integral
      #    IS the counterfactual directly — do NOT add car-solar (that would
      #    double-count). Monotone within the day, so the tier flag latches once.
      - name: "EV Counterfactual Daily Export"
        unique_id: ev_counterfactual_daily_export
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.ev_daily_grid_export') | float(0) }}

      # -- Tier split of solar-to-car power (ISC-17, ISC-18) ------------------
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier1 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf < lim else 0 }}
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier2 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf >= lim else 0 }}

      # -- Health check: hardware total vs sum of split integrals -------------
      #    Should track ~0. A growing residual means a dropout is skewing the
      #    integral-derived ratio (the billed $ is still safe — it's anchored to
      #    hardware — but the split may be off).
      - name: "EV Split Residual kWh"
        unique_id: ev_split_residual_kwh
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set hw = states('sensor.ev_car_energy_int_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {{ (hw - (s + g)) | round(3) }}

      # -- Hardware-anchored billed split, MONTH (ISC-22 inputs) -------------
      #    billed total (hardware) rescaled by the integral-derived ratio.
      - name: "EV Solar kWh Month"
        unique_id: ev_solar_kwh_month
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {{ (total * (s / d) if d > 0 else 0) | round(3) }}
      - name: "EV Grid kWh Month"
        unique_id: ev_grid_kwh_month
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {{ (total * (g / d) if d > 0 else total) | round(3) }}

      # -- Cost sensors (ISC-22, ISC-23) -------------------------------------
      #    cost = billed_tier1×fit1 + billed_tier2×fit2 + billed_grid×consump.
      #    Billed portions = hardware total × integral-derived fractions. No
      #    hardcoded tariff anywhere (ISC-38). Unit chain: kWh × $/kWh = $.
      - name: "EV Cost Month"
        unique_id: ev_cost_month
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:cash
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s  = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly')  | float(0) %}
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {% set solar_frac = (s / d) if d > 0 else 0 %}
          {% set billed_solar = total * solar_frac %}
          {% set billed_grid  = total * (1 - solar_frac) %}
          {% set ts = t1 + t2 %}
          {% set t1_frac = (t1 / ts) if ts > 0 else 0 %}
          {{ (billed_solar * t1_frac * r1
              + billed_solar * (1 - t1_frac) * r2
              + billed_grid * rg) | round(2) }}
      - name: "EV Cost Today"
        unique_id: ev_cost_today
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:cash-clock
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set s  = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_daily')  | float(0) %}
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {% set solar_frac = (s / d) if d > 0 else 0 %}
          {% set billed_solar = total * solar_frac %}
          {% set billed_grid  = total * (1 - solar_frac) %}
          {% set ts = t1 + t2 %}
          {% set t1_frac = (t1 / ts) if ts > 0 else 0 %}
          {{ (billed_solar * t1_frac * r1
              + billed_solar * (1 - t1_frac) * r2
              + billed_grid * rg) | round(2) }}

      # -- Last completed month (from utility_meter last_period attribute) ----
      - name: "EV Billed Energy Last Month"
        unique_id: ev_billed_energy_last_month
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {{ state_attr('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly','last_period') | float(0) | round(3) }}
      - name: "EV Cost Last Month"
        unique_id: ev_cost_last_month
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:cash-clock
        state: >
          {% set total = state_attr('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly','last_period') | float(0) %}
          {% set s  = state_attr('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly','last_period') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = state_attr('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly','last_period')  | float(0) %}
          {% set t1 = state_attr('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly','last_period') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = state_attr('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly','last_period') | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {% set solar_frac = (s / d) if d > 0 else 0 %}
          {% set billed_solar = total * solar_frac %}
          {% set billed_grid  = total * (1 - solar_frac) %}
          {% set ts = t1 + t2 %}
          {% set t1_frac = (t1 / ts) if ts > 0 else 0 %}
          {{ (billed_solar * t1_frac * r1
              + billed_solar * (1 - t1_frac) * r2
              + billed_grid * rg) | round(2) }}

      # -- Cumulative (all-time) $ — drives session cost by snapshot diff -----
      #    Uses the all-time integrals (which never reset), so a session that
      #    straddles midnight or crosses the FIT tier is handled exactly.
      - name: "EV Cost Cumulative"
        unique_id: ev_cost_cumulative
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total_increasing
        state: >
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh')        | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {{ (t1*r1 + t2*r2 + g*rg) | round(4) }}

      # -- Session energy & cost by snapshot differencing (ISC-24, ISC-25) ---
      - name: "EV Session Energy kWh"
        unique_id: ev_session_energy_kwh
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set now = states('sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy') | float(0) %}
          {% set start = states('input_number.ev_session_energy_start') | float(0) %}
          {{ [now - start, 0] | max | round(3) }}
      - name: "EV Session Cost"
        unique_id: ev_session_cost
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:car-electric
        state: >
          {% set now = states('sensor.ev_cost_cumulative') | float(0) %}
          {% set start = states('input_number.ev_session_cost_start') | float(0) %}
          {{ [now - start, 0] | max | round(2) }}

  - binary_sensor:
      # -- Session state (ISC-26) — debounced ---------------------------------
      - name: "EV Charging Active"
        unique_id: ev_charging_active
        device_class: battery_charging
        delay_on: "00:00:20"     # debounce start
        delay_off: "00:02:00"    # debounce end (BYD taper / brief dropouts)
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) > 100 }}

# ===========================================================================
# 3. RIEMANN INTEGRALS  (ISC-8, ISC-13, ISC-14, ISC-19)
#    method: left, kWh. max_sub_interval advances the integral on a timer so a
#    frozen source doesn't silently stall it (advisor hardening). These drive
#    the solar:grid RATIO; billed kWh comes from the hardware register (§4).
# ===========================================================================
sensor:
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_car_power_w
    name: "EV Car Energy Int kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_energy_int_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Solar kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_grid_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Grid kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_grid_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier1 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier2 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  # Exportable solar surplus energy (Option B) — feeds the daily FIT tier meter.
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_grid_export_w
    name: "EV Grid Export Energy kWh"
    unique_id: ev_grid_export_energy_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3

# ===========================================================================
# 4. UTILITY METERS  (ISC-15, ISC-20, ISC-21)
#    Daily + monthly. Billed energy is metered off the plug's HARDWARE total
#    (drift-free). The integral meters below feed the solar:grid ratio only.
#    NOTE: monthly meters reset on the 1st — this is for Nick's own accounting,
#    not aligned to the retailer's billing period.
# ===========================================================================
utility_meter:
  # Billed energy — HARDWARE register (source of truth for kWh billed)
  ev_billed_energy_daily:   { source: sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy, cycle: daily }
  ev_billed_energy_monthly: { source: sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy, cycle: monthly }

  # Daily exportable solar surplus (Option B) — feeds the FIT tier boundary.
  #   Sourced from the surplus integral above (PV − baseline), NOT a grid meter.
  ev_daily_grid_export:
    source: sensor.ev_grid_export_energy_kwh
    cycle: daily

  # Integral-derived ratio meters (NOT billed directly)
  ev_car_solar_daily:    { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_monthly:  { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_grid_daily:     { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_grid_monthly:   { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_solar_tier1_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: monthly }

# ===========================================================================
# 5. COST SENSORS  — defined inside the single `template:` block in §2
#    (HA forbids two top-level `template:` keys in one package file).
# ===========================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# 6. AUTOMATIONS
# ===========================================================================
automation:
  # --- Session snapshot on charge start (ISC-24, ISC-25) -------------------
  # Records the hardware-energy and cumulative-cost anchors; the session
  # sensors read the difference from "now".
  - id: ev_session_snapshot
    alias: "EV — snapshot session anchors on charge start"
    mode: single
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: binary_sensor.ev_charging_active
        from: "off"
        to: "on"
    actions:
      - action: input_number.set_value
        target: { entity_id: input_number.ev_session_energy_start }
        data:
          value: "{{ states('sensor.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy') | float(0) }}"
      - action: input_number.set_value
        target: { entity_id: input_number.ev_session_cost_start }
        data:
          value: "{{ states('sensor.ev_cost_cumulative') | float(0) }}"

  # --- Solar-following: turn ON (ISC-27, ISC-30) ---------------------------
  # DORMANT: initial_state false + gated on ev_solar_charge_mode. Fires when the
  # estimated exportable surplus (PV − baseline) exceeds the car's ~2.3 kW draw
  # for a sustained 10 min, so the plug only switches on when solar can cover it.
  - id: ev_solar_follow_on
    alias: "EV — solar follow: turn plug ON"
    mode: single
    initial_state: false
    triggers:
      - trigger: numeric_state
        entity_id: sensor.ev_grid_export_w
        above: 2300
        for: "00:10:00"
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
        state: "on"
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch
        state: "off"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_on
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch }

  # --- Solar-following: turn OFF (ISC-28, ISC-30) --------------------------
  # No grid-import sensor on this system, so we switch OFF when the exportable
  # surplus falls below ~1.5 kW (a deadband under the 2.3 kW ON trigger, which
  # prevents oscillation) for a sustained 10 min. Tune the 1500 to taste.
  - id: ev_solar_follow_off
    alias: "EV — solar follow: turn plug OFF"
    mode: single
    initial_state: false
    triggers:
      - trigger: numeric_state
        entity_id: sensor.ev_grid_export_w
        below: 1500          # surplus floor (W) — deadband below the ON trigger
        for: "00:10:00"
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
        state: "on"
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        state: "off"         # never fight a manual force-on
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch
        state: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_off
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch }

  # --- Manual force-on override (ISC-29) -----------------------------------
  - id: ev_charge_now_force
    alias: "EV — charge now: force plug ON"
    mode: single
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        to: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_on
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch }

# Interceptor — Stealth Browser Automation

**Tool:** `interceptor` CLI — Chrome extension that controls the real browser from the inside.
**Repo:** https://github.com/Hacker-Valley-Media/slop-browser
**Install:** `~/Projects/interceptor` (built from source — see `Workflows/Update.md`)

### Why Interceptor?

agent-browser (the Browser skill) uses CDP — sites can detect it. Interceptor is a Chrome extension that operates through the actual browser UI. No debugger, no automation flags, no separate browser instance. You stay logged in, you pass bot detection, the agent sees what you see.

### Prerequisites

- Chrome or Brave running with the Interceptor extension loaded
- `interceptor` CLI in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor`)
- `interceptor-daemon` in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor-daemon`)
- Native messaging manifest registered (`bash ~/Projects/interceptor/scripts/install.sh --chrome --skip-extension`)
- (Optional, macOS) `interceptor-bridge` helper app — see "Bridge" section below

### Remote Execution — Linux box → Mac over SSH (REQUIRED on the Linux host)

Interceptor is a Chrome extension; it only runs where a real, logged-in Chrome
is. The Linux workstation has **no Chrome and no interceptor binary** — do not
try to install or run it locally there. Instead, drive the interceptor that
already lives on the Mac (where Nick stays logged into Seek, LinkedIn, etc.)
over SSH. The Mac is reachable as the `mac` / `nicholass-macbook-pro` SSH alias.

Prefix every interceptor command with the SSH hop and the Homebrew PATH (the
non-interactive SSH shell does not inherit `/opt/homebrew/bin`):

```bash
# Preflight: confirm the Mac, daemon, and Chrome are all up
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor status; pgrep -lf "Google Chrome" | head -1'

# Any interceptor command, run on the Mac's real browser:
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor open "https://www.seek.com.au/my-activity/saved-jobs" --text-only'
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor scroll bottom; interceptor wait 1500; interceptor text | tail -90'
```

Wrap long output in `| head`/`| tail` to keep it bounded. Use `timeout 90 ssh …`
so a hung page can't stall the turn. Everything else in this skill works
unchanged once you've prefixed the SSH hop — refs, compound commands, network
log, scene graph all behave identically; they just execute on the Mac.

### Bridge — macOS Native Helper App

The bridge is an optional Swift helper that runs as a LaunchAgent and unlocks
capabilities the Chrome extension can't provide on its own: OS-level synthetic
input (`act --os`), accessibility tree of native macOS apps, app control,
clipboard, screen capture beyond Chrome, audio/speech, files, notifications,
HealthKit, Apple Intelligence. ~95% of typical work doesn't need it.

**Status check:** `interceptor status` reports `bridge: running` with PID + socket
when it's up, or `bridge: not running` when it isn't.

**Lifecycle (install / verify / troubleshoot / uninstall) lives entirely in
`Workflows/Update.md` section 6.** Future updates flow through the Update
workflow — never reach for the upstream `install-bridge.sh` directly; that
script breaks on Apple Silicon (`/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, but sudoing the
whole script makes `launchctl bootstrap` target uid 0 instead of the user).
The skill's procedure is the canonical one.

**Security model — read before installing:**

- Transport is a **UNIX domain socket** at `/tmp/interceptor-bridge.sock`.
  Local-only; no network listener; not reachable from another machine.
- **No authentication on the socket.** Any local process running as your user
  can connect and execute every bridge action — including synthetic input,
  clipboard read, audio capture, screenshots. macOS TCC permissions
  (Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording, Microphone) are granted
  to the bridge once and inherited by every socket client.
- **Marginal risk is supply-chain:** a malicious package installed via
  bun/brew/npm gains a one-step path to OS-level input/screen/clipboard without
  needing its own permission grants — the bridge has them.
- Single-user Mac threat model: acceptable, since anything running as you can
  already do this with effort. Multi-user Macs need socket hardening (see
  Update.md section 6c).
- Binary built locally from `~/Projects/interceptor/interceptor-bridge/Sources/`,
  not a downloaded prebuilt. Provenance is Swift source we just compiled.

## Compound Commands (Preferred)

These collapse multi-step patterns into single invocations — fewer tool calls, fewer tokens:

```bash
interceptor open "https://example.com"              # Open URL, wait, return tree + text
interceptor open <url> --tree-only|--text-only|--full|--no-wait
interceptor read                                     # Tree + text for active tab
interceptor read <ref>                               # Tree + text for element subtree
interceptor read --include-style|--include-frames
interceptor act <ref>                                # Click + wait + return updated tree + diff
interceptor act <ref> "value"                        # Type + wait + return updated tree
interceptor act <ref> --os                           # OS-level trusted input (requires bridge)
interceptor act <ref> --keys "Enter"                 # Send keyboard shortcut
interceptor inspect                                  # Tree + text + network log + headers
interceptor inspect --net-only                       # Network only
```

## Core Commands

```bash
# State + discovery
interceptor state [--full]              # DOM tree + metadata
interceptor tree [--filter all] [--depth N] [--max-chars N]
interceptor diff                         # Changes since last state/tree read
interceptor find "query" [--role button] # Find elements by name
interceptor text [<index|ref>]
interceptor html <index|ref>

# Element interaction
interceptor click <ref>                  # Click by ref (eN)
interceptor click <ref> --at X,Y         # Click at coordinates
interceptor dblclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor rightclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor type <ref> <text> [--append]
interceptor type "role:name" <text>      # Semantic selector
interceptor select <ref> <value>         # Dropdown
interceptor focus|hover <ref>
interceptor drag <ref> --from X,Y --to X,Y [--steps N] [--duration MS]
interceptor keys "<combo>"               # e.g. "Control+A"

# Navigation + tabs
interceptor navigate <url>
interceptor back | forward
interceptor scroll <up|down|top|bottom>
interceptor wait <ms> | wait-stable [--ms N] [--timeout N]
interceptor tabs
interceptor tab new [url] | tab close [id] | tab switch <id>

# Capture
interceptor screenshot [--save] [--format png|jpeg] [--full] [--clip X,Y,W,H] [--element N]
interceptor eval <code> [--main]         # JS in isolated or main world
interceptor capture start | frame | stop # tabCapture stream

# Style injection (test redesigns live)
interceptor style inject --css "<rules>" [--top-only]
interceptor style remove <handle>

# Cookies
interceptor cookies <domain>
interceptor cookies set <json>
interceptor cookies delete <url> <name>
```

## Network

```bash
# Passive capture (always-on, no CDP fingerprint)
interceptor net log [--filter <pat>] [--limit N] [--since <ts>]
interceptor net headers [--filter <pat>]   # CSRF, auth headers
interceptor net clear

# Request override (passive, no CDP)
interceptor override "*pattern*" key=value
interceptor override clear

# CDP-attached interception (explicit opt-in — leaves debugger banner)
interceptor network on [patterns...]
interceptor network off
interceptor network log
interceptor network override on '<json>'
interceptor network override off

# SSE streams (LLM responses, live feeds)
interceptor sse log [--filter <pat>] [--limit N]
interceptor sse streams
interceptor sse tail [--filter <pat>]

# Header rewriting
interceptor headers add <name> <value>
interceptor headers remove <name>
interceptor headers clear
```

## Recording (Session Monitor)

Record real user actions on the active tab, replay as a deterministic plan script.

```bash
interceptor monitor start ["instruction"]   # Start recording
interceptor monitor pause | resume
interceptor monitor stop                     # End + emit summary
interceptor monitor status [--all]
interceptor monitor list                     # All sessions
interceptor monitor tail [--current] [--raw] # Live tail
interceptor monitor export <sessionId>       # Aligned text
interceptor monitor export <sessionId> --plan # Replay script
interceptor monitor export <sessionId> --json
```

## Canvas (Rich Web Apps)

For apps that render to `<canvas>` (Figma, Excalidraw, in-house editors):

```bash
interceptor canvas list | status
interceptor canvas log [N] [--kind fillText]
interceptor canvas objects [N] [--kind text]
interceptor canvas model | routes
interceptor canvas ocr N [--region X,Y,W,H]
interceptor canvas read N [--format png] [--region X,Y,W,H] [--webgl]
interceptor canvas diff <url1> <url2> [--threshold 10] [--image]
```

## Scene Graph (Rich Editors — Google Docs/Slides, Canva)

```bash
interceptor scene profile [--verbose]
interceptor scene list [--type shape|text|image|page|embed|slide]
interceptor scene click <id> | dblclick <id> | select <id>
interceptor scene hit <x> <y>                # ID object at coordinates
interceptor scene selected | text [--with-html]
interceptor scene insert "<text>"
interceptor scene cursor-to <x> <y>
interceptor scene slide list | current | goto <index> | notes [--slide N]
interceptor scene render <id> [--save]
interceptor scene zoom
interceptor scene ... --profile <name>       # Force profile, bypass detection
```

## LinkedIn

```bash
interceptor linkedin event [url]             # Event + post data via DOM + network
interceptor linkedin attendees [url]         # Attendees with override + enrichment
```

## ChatGPT Agentic Bridge

Drive chatgpt.com from CLI without an API key:

```bash
interceptor chatgpt send "<prompt>" [--stream]
interceptor chatgpt read | status
interceptor chatgpt conversations | switch <id>
interceptor chatgpt model [name]
interceptor chatgpt stop
```

## Batch + Meta

```bash
interceptor batch '<json_array>' [--stop-on-error] [--timeout MS]
interceptor status                    # Daemon + bridge state (local check)
interceptor help
```

## Key Rules

- **Requires Chrome running** — it's an extension, not a standalone binary.
- **Refs use eN syntax** — `e12` not `@e12`. No `@` prefix.
- **Cross-frame refs** — `read --include-frames` returns refs like `e<frameId>_<n>` for non-top frames.
- **`--json`** is a global flag for structured output.
- **Daemon auto-starts** — first command launches it; no manual start needed.
- **Bridge is optional** — only needed for `act --os` and OS-trusted input. Without it, interceptor falls back to in-page synthetic events.

## Delegating to Agents

When spawning agents for Interceptor work:

```
Agent(subagent_type="general-purpose", prompt="
  Use interceptor CLI for all browser work.
  Commands: open <url>, read, act eN, act eN 'text', inspect, screenshot.
  Compound commands preferred — they return tree + text in one call.
  Refs use eN syntax (no @ prefix) from tree output.
  Use --json for structured output.
  [your specific task instructions here]
")
```

## Gotchas

- **Screenshot ignores scroll position.** `interceptor screenshot` (with or without `--full`) captures from y=0 of the document — it does not honor `window.scrollTo`, `scrollIntoView`, `scroll bottom`, or `keys End`. For tall pages, content below the fold is unreachable through screenshot. Workaround: render the section of interest at its own short URL (`/problems.html`, `/section-3.html`) and screenshot that page directly. The `--clip "x,y,w,h"` flag returns "Cannot read properties of undefined" — broken in the current build. *(2026-04-27)*
- **Multiple tabs at the same URL confuse routing.** When two tabs both load `localhost:5180/`, `tab switch <id>` reports `ok` but the visually-active Chrome tab may not change, and `screenshot` captures whatever Chrome is showing — not what `interceptor text` and `interceptor navigate` are routing to. Close duplicate tabs before screenshotting, or always work from a freshly-opened single tab.
- **`eval` is CSP-blocked on most sites.** Use `eval --main` to run in the page's main world instead of the isolated extension world. Even with `--main`, sites with strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) will still block string-eval; pass small expressions only and avoid `Function`-constructor patterns.
- **MV3 service worker idles in seconds — wake it and act in ONE SSH session.** "error: no extensions connected" usually means the extension's service worker went idle, not that the install broke. Wake it by opening a window in its profile (`open -na "Google Chrome" --args --profile-directory="Profile 3"`), sleep ~5s, then chain ALL interceptor commands in the same SSH invocation — a follow-up `ssh` call ~10s later will find the worker asleep again. *(2026-08-23)*
- **No Chrome / no binary on the Linux box — run on the Mac over SSH.** `which interceptor` returns nothing on the Linux workstation and there is no Chrome/Brave/Chromium installed there, so the skill appears "broken" if you try to run it locally. It is not broken — it lives on the Mac. Hop to it: `ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor <cmd>'`. The `export PATH` is mandatory (non-interactive SSH shells miss `/opt/homebrew/bin`). See "Remote Execution" under Prerequisites. *(2026-06-16)*

name: reference-ha-read-via-interceptor-callws
description: How to read Home Assistant data (states, long-term statistics) with no API token, via Nick's logged-in Chrome on the Mac and hass.callWS through Interceptor
metadata:
  type: reference
---

No HA long-lived token exists on either machine (grep-verified Aug and Oct 2026). Working path: Nick logs into HA in the Mac Chrome profile Interceptor controls (he did on 2026-10-11, "Keep me logged in"), then:

```
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH; interceptor navigate "http://homeassistant.local:8123/"; interceptor wait 4000; interceptor eval --main "<js>"'
```

- States: `document.querySelector("home-assistant").hass.states[id]`.
- Long-term stats (survive the 10-day recorder purge): `hass.callWS({type:"recorder/statistics_during_period", start_time, end_time, statistic_ids:[...], period:"day", types:["state","sum"]})`. Promise, so stash to `window.__r` then read in a second eval after `interceptor wait 3000`, all in ONE ssh call.
- Day buckets start at 14:00Z (midnight AEST). `state` = last value in bucket.
- EV spend for a window = `sensor.ev_cost_cumulative` end minus start. `sensor.ev_cost_last_month` is the dashboard's official prior-month figure (recomputed at current tariffs, so it can differ by cents).
- Package went live 6 Sep 2026; plug energy from 4 to 6 Sep (~23.7 kWh) is not in any cost sensor and was handled by Nick's manual backdate ($2.98 gross, +$0.48 net). See [[project-ev-charging-sept-2026-spend]].

**How to apply:** if the page shows "Welcome home!" the session is gone; ask Nick to log in again rather than hunting for a token.

content.text:
Verified: both HA methods agree to within six cents, the daily deltas sum to the cumulative total, and the hardware kWh register reconciles with the billed-energy meter. Nothing else to fetch.

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: Nick logged into HA on the Mac after my first attempt hit the login page.

📃 CONTENT:

**Car charging spend, 31 Aug to 30 Sep 2026, per Home Assistant: $15.12.**

| Measure | Value |
|---------|-------|
| HA official September figure (`ev_cost_last_month`) | $15.12 |
| Same window via cumulative cost sensor, end minus start | $15.06 |
| Energy billed by HA (6 to 30 Sep) | 106.96 kWh |
| Plug hardware register, lifetime to 30 Sep | 130.57 kWh |
| Tariffs in force | grid 24.92c, solar tier 1 8c, tier 2 2c per kWh |

The six-cent gap is the consumption tariff moving from 24c to 24.92c part way through the month. The last-month sensor recomputes at today's rate, the cumulative sensor accrued at the rate of the day. Use $15.12, it is what the dashboard shows.

**Two caveats on the window edges.**

- **31 Aug to 4 Sep has no data.** The plug was not installed until 4 Sep. Nothing can be read for those days.
